acceptance_criteria.given: an inventory update has just been committed for a department with regulatory ledger control ('DGDAIFLG' = '1'), and the system prompts to print the ledger

acceptance_criteria.then: the system generates the ledger report, sends it to the printer, saves a print job record with a job ID, and displays a confirmation including the job ID

acceptance_criteria.given: the prompt to print the ledger appears
acceptance_criteria.when: the user declines the print dialog
acceptance_criteria.then: no print job is created, and the workflow continues normally

acceptance_criteria.given: an inventory update occurs in a department that is not regulated for ledgers

acceptance_criteria.then: the prompt to print the ledger is never shown, and no print job is recorded

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Ledger print jobs must be logged with a timestamp and operator identity to satisfy audit requirements.

features.title: Warehouse Code (Hokanko) Direct Entry and Selection
features.description: Enables users to enter a warehouse code directly by typing into a DataWindow or select from a lookup list via double-click or Select button, with server-side existence validation. The selected code is returned to the calling parent screen for downstream business processes.
features.source: SRS UIBlueprint w_pop_devhokanko, S.5 Events #1-#6 (focal entrypoint)

functions.label: Type a warehouse code for real-time validation (dw_hokanko)
functions.description: Allows the user to type a warehouse code directly into the entry field. The system immediately validates the entered code against the server using the current devCode context. If the code+devCode combination is not found, a message box alerts the user.

functions.label: Open warehouse selector by double-clicking grid (w_pop_devhokanko_sheet)
functions.description: Double-clicking the data grid opens a modal popup listing all warehouses. The popup displays a full, unfiltered warehouse list irrespective of the current development code. Once the user picks a value, the code is fed back into the entry field and validated.

functions.label: Confirm selection with Enter key (TriggerEvent(doubleclicked!))
functions.description: Pressing the Enter key while a row is focused in the grid simulates a double-click action. This confirms the currently highlighted warehouse and proceeds with the selection. It provides a keyboard-driven alternative to the mouse double-click.

functions.label: Choose highlighted warehouse and close popup (GetSelectedRow(0))
functions.description: Clicking the Select button reads the currently highlighted row from the grid and closes the popup, returning the warehouse data. If no row is selected, it returns a blank result. This provides an explicit confirmation path independent of double-click or Enter key.

functions.label: Cancel warehouse entry and close popup (Close button)
functions.description: Clicking the Close button dismisses the popup without saving any selected warehouse code. It returns a blank hokankocd value, effectively cancelling the operation. No confirmation dialog is shown before closing.

functions.label: Forward window key press to deferred event (pbm_dwnkey)
functions.description: The window captures every raw Windows key message and posts it as an asynchronous deferred event. The actual handling logic resides in a separate key event (likely ancestor-level) and is not visible. This mechanism enables centralized keyboard input processing.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder popup window (w_pop_devhokanko) where the user enters a warehouse code (hokanko) by typing directly into a DataWindow or selecting from a list via a modal lookup, with synchronous server-side validation of code existence. Selection can be confirmed via double-click, Enter key, or Select button, and cancelled with the Close button.
business_context.target_state: A React modal component (<WarehouseCodeSelector />) backed by GET /api/v1/warehouses for retrieving the unfiltered list and POST /api/v1/warehouses/validate for real-time existence validation, with keyboard-accessible selection and focus management.

success_criteria: Warehouse code existence validation must respond within 1 second to avoid blocking the UI during synchronous server lookup.

user_stories.title: Validate Warehouse Code Direct Entry
user_stories.i_want_to: type a warehouse code directly into the entry field and have it immediately validated against the system
user_stories.so_that: I can quickly enter a known warehouse code without browsing a list and be confident it is a valid code before proceeding

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has a valid warehouse code for the currently selected development room
acceptance_criteria.when: the user types the code into the entry field and moves focus away
acceptance_criteria.then: the system confirms the code exists, displays the corresponding warehouse name, and sets the internal return value with the valid code

acceptance_criteria.given: the user types a warehouse code that does not exist for the current development room
acceptance_criteria.when: the user moves focus away from the entry field
acceptance_criteria.then: the system shows an error message '入力した保管庫は存在しません。' and clears the warehouse code and name fields without persisting the invalid code

acceptance_criteria.given: the user clears the warehouse code field
acceptance_criteria.when: the user moves focus away
acceptance_criteria.then: the system clears the display of the warehouse name and the internal mirror value without throwing a validation error

user_stories.technical_notes: Implemented in uo_hokan_hokankocd.u_post_itemchange event. Uses embedded SQL SELECT INTO against FATRA transaction object to check existence of code+devCode combination. On failure, sets il_rtn=1, shows MessageBox('保管庫','入力した保管庫は存在しません。'), and clears the field. On success, populates warehouse name via SetItem and mirrors to sle_code.
user_stories.migration_hint: Replace with REST call GET /api/v1/warehouses/validate?devCode={devCode}&warehouseCode={code} to check existence. Use controlled input component with debounced validation.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All database queries must use parameterised statements to prevent SQL injection, as legacy embedded SQL uses variable substitution.

user_stories.title: Select Warehouse Code from Popup List
user_stories.i_want_to: browse a list of warehouse codes in a popup, select one, and have that code returned to the calling screen
user_stories.so_that: I can choose a warehouse code even when I do not know the exact code, ensuring I pick a valid entry from all available options

acceptance_criteria.given: the popup is open and displays a list of warehouse codes with associated development room details, and a row is highlighted
acceptance_criteria.when: the user confirms the selection by double‑clicking the row, pressing the Enter key, or clicking the Select button
acceptance_criteria.then: the popup closes and returns the selected warehouse code and its development room code to the parent screen

acceptance_criteria.given: the popup is open and the user does not want to make a selection
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Close button
acceptance_criteria.then: the popup closes and returns a blank warehouse code, signalling that no selection was made

acceptance_criteria.given: the system has no warehouse codes to display
acceptance_criteria.when: the user opens the popup
acceptance_criteria.then: a message 'データがありません。' is displayed to inform the user there are no warehouse codes available

acceptance_criteria.given: the popup has data but no row is highlighted (e.g., the user deselects or scrolls away without picking a row)
acceptance_criteria.when: the user attempts to confirm with the Select button or double‑click
acceptance_criteria.then: the popup closes and returns a blank warehouse code, treating the action as a cancellation

user_stories.technical_notes: Hosted in w_pop_devhokanko_sheet (window). Binds DataWindow dw_devhokan_hokanko_sheet to FATRA transaction object. On open, Retrieve() loads all warehouse rows for 'representative' dev-rooms (join on gpcd, filter DGDAIFLG='1'), auto-selects row 1. Double-clicked event extends ancestor via call super:: and returns selected devcd/hokankocd via CloseWithReturn. Enter key (dwnkey event) triggers doubleclicked! synchronously. Select button (cb_applay) reads GetSelectedRow(0) and follows the same return logic. Close button sets s_hokankocd to blank and returns. Window-level u_dwnkey forwards pbm_dwnkey via PostEvent(key!). Empty result set handled with MessageBox('検索','データがありません。').
user_stories.migration_hint: Implement as a React modal component (<WarehouseCodeSelector />) that calls POST /api/v1/warehouses/ledger-search to populate the grid. Provide keyboard navigation, double‑click/Enter selection, and a cancel button. Return selected code via onSelect callback or reject via onCancel.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: The popup must enforce JWT‑based authentication and authorisation, ensuring only authorised users can browse warehouse codes (legacy had no access control).

features.title: Person-in-Charge Code Lookup and Selection
features.description: Provides a popup lookup window triggered by a host DataWindow double‑click on a person‑in‑charge code field, enabling the user to search, validate, and select a responsible person via a list backed by existence checks.
features.source: SRS UIBlueprint for uo_hokan_syainno user object, covering S.5 Events #1–#7 (host DataWindow double‑click, existence check, popup open, Enter‑key confirmation, row double‑click, select/close button actions).

functions.label: Validate person-in-charge code against master data (u_post_itemchange)
functions.description: When a user enters a person-in-charge code, the system checks its existence by querying the M_SYAKAN and M_TANTOKAN tables. This ensures only valid codes are accepted, preventing errors and providing immediate feedback during data entry.

functions.label: Open person-in-charge lookup popup and pre-select first entry (w_pop_syainno.open)
functions.description: The system opens a popup window displaying all eligible persons-in-charge, with the first row automatically selected to streamline selection. This speeds up the lookup process for the user.

functions.label: Launch lookup from code field and apply returned selection (dw_syain.doubleclicked)
functions.description: When a user double-clicks the person-in-charge code field in the host window, a lookup popup appears. After the user selects a person, the chosen code is passed back to trigger the validation process, integrating lookup with data validation seamlessly.

functions.label: Confirm selection with Enter key on popup row (dw_1.dwnkey)
functions.description: In the person-in-charge popup, pressing Enter while a row is highlighted acts as a confirmation, simulating a double-click. This closes the popup and finalizes the selection, providing a keyboard shortcut for efficiency.

functions.label: Select person by double-clicking popup row (dw_1.doubleclicked)
functions.description: When the user double-clicks a row in the person-in-charge popup list, that row is chosen as the selection. The popup closes and the code is used for subsequent processing, offering a direct method to pick a person.

functions.label: Confirm highlighted row with Select button (cb_applay.clicked)
functions.description: By clicking the Select button, the user confirms the currently highlighted row in the popup, even if it was not double-clicked. The selection is finalized and the popup closes, allowing explicit confirmation.

functions.label: Cancel lookup without selecting (cb_close.clicked)
functions.description: Clicking the Close button dismisses the person-in-charge popup without selecting any person. No changes are applied to the original field, allowing the user to abort the lookup operation.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder user object (uo_hokan_syainno) that provides a person‑in‑charge lookup popup. The host DataWindow (dw_syain) double‑click triggers the popup (w_pop_syainno) to display eligible persons, with code validation and row selection via double‑click or button click.
business_context.target_state: A React lookup component (<PersonInChargeLookup />) integrated into modern forms, backed by GET /api/v1/persons‑in‑charge?code= for existence validation, and a modal popup for selection with keyboard and button confirmation.

success_criteria: Lookup popup must open within 1 second of triggering to maintain smooth user flow.
All database queries must use parameterised statements to prevent SQL injection (dynamic SQL detected in person‑in‑charge existence check).

features.title: Deposit Name Selection via Container Lookup Popup
features.description: Enables users to search and select a deposit name (container name) from a distinct list of containers displayed in a popup grid, and confirm the selection by double‑click, Enter key, or Select button, or cancel with the Close button.

functions.label: Retrieve and auto-select the first deposit name on popup open (Window Open)
functions.description: When the deposit name lookup popup opens, the system loads a distinct list of container names and automatically highlights the first row. If no names are retrieved, an alert message informs the user. This ensures the user can immediately see and select from available deposit names without manual navigation.

functions.label: Confirm selection with Enter key on grid (Enter Key Press on Grid)
functions.description: While the grid has focus, pressing the Enter key simulates a double-click on the current row, confirming the selected deposit name. This provides a convenient keyboard shortcut, allowing users to complete the selection without using the mouse.

functions.label: Confirm deposit name via row double-click (Row Double-Click)
functions.description: Double-clicking any grid row immediately confirms that deposit name as the selection and closes the popup, returning the value to the calling window. This mouse-driven action lets users rapidly pick a name without extra confirmation steps.

functions.label: Confirm highlighted deposit name via Select button (Select Button Click)
functions.description: Clicking the Select button confirms the currently highlighted row and closes the popup with its value. If no row is highlighted, an empty string is returned. The button offers an explicit action for users who prefer clicking to double-clicking or pressing Enter.

functions.label: Cancel deposit name lookup without selection (Close Button Click)
functions.description: Clicking the Close button dismisses the popup without confirming any deposit name and returns an empty string to the parent window. This allows the user to abandon the lookup process with no changes or data returned.

features.title: Product Code (Syohincd) Lookup and Selection
features.description: Popup window enabling users to search for reagent product codes by entering a name filter, browse matching results in a grid, and select a product code to return to the calling window.

functions.label: Initialize empty search field on popup open (Window Open)
functions.description: When the product code lookup popup window opens, the search input field is automatically cleared. The results grid remains empty until the user performs a search, ensuring a fresh start without residual data.

functions.label: Search for reagent products by name (Search Button Click)
functions.description: The user enters a product name filter and clicks the Search button to retrieve a list of matching reagent products. If no records are found, a message box informs the user that zero results were returned.

functions.label: Repost window key-press for deferred handling (Window-Level Key Relay)
functions.description: When a key is pressed while the popup window has focus, the system reposts the message as a deferred key event. This enables asynchronous keyboard input handling, though the specific keycodes involved are not defined in the source.

functions.label: Select product code by double-clicking a grid row (Grid Row Double-Click)
functions.description: Double-clicking a row in the search results grid captures that row's product code and closes the popup, returning the selection to the parent window. The action requires a valid row (index greater than zero).

functions.label: Select product code with Enter key in grid (Grid Enter-Key Selection)
functions.description: While the search results grid has focus, pressing the Enter key selects the focused row's product code and closes the popup. This mimics the double-click behavior for keyboard-driven selection.

functions.label: Apply selected product code with Apply button (Apply/Select Button Click)
functions.description: The user clicks the Apply button to return the product code from the currently selected grid row to the calling window. A row must be selected beforehand for the action to succeed.

functions.label: Cancel lookup without selecting a product code (Close Button Click)
functions.description: Clicking the Close button dismisses the popup and returns an empty result, allowing the user to exit the product code lookup without making a selection. No preconditions are required.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder popup window (w_pub_pop_syohincd_e) where users enter a product name filter in a text field, click Search to populate a DataWindow grid (dw_1) with matching reagent product records, and select a product code by double-clicking a row, pressing Enter, or clicking the Apply button. The Cancel button closes without selection.
business_context.target_state: A React popup component (<ProductCodeLookup />) backed by a REST endpoint GET /api/v1/reagent-products?name={filter} that returns matching results in a keyboard-navigable grid, with double-click, Enter key, and Apply button selection, and a Cancel button to dismiss without selection.

results.module_business_description: Governs the lifecycle tracking, subdivision, stocktaking, and regulatory documentation of chemical inventories across development storage locations. Ensures compliance with poison and deleterious substance controls through batch and lot management, weight monitoring, and integrated ledger reporting.

features.title: Stock (Zaiko) List Search, Export, Print, and Custodian Bulk Reassignment
features.description: Enables warehouse operators to search stock items by storage code, employee, and department criteria; view stock and movement history across tabs; export results to Excel; print Poison/Deleterious Substances Ledgers; and perform bulk or selected-row custodian (tanto) reassignment via popups, with field-level validation.
features.source: SRS UIBlueprint w_hokanko_zaiko_list, S.1 screen identity and S.5 Events #1-#15

functions.label: Search stock items using filter criteria (Search)
functions.description: The warehouse operator triggers a stock search based on the applied storage code, employee, and department filters. The system retrieves matching stock records and displays them in the stock list, also clearing any previously displayed movement history tab content. If an Excel export session is active, the export sheet is automatically refreshed with the new search results.

functions.label: Export the current stock list to an Excel file (Excel Export)
functions.description: The user can export the currently displayed stock list data to an Excel file. This action uses a predefined dataset from the stock list display and invokes the Excel/CSV save functionality. It provides a convenient way to share or analyze inventory data outside the system.

functions.label: Open the poison/deleterious substances ledger print screen (Ledger Print)
functions.description: The warehouse operator accesses the print screen for regulated substance ledgers. This triggers a modal window where the operator can configure and print the official ledger records for poisonous and deleterious substances, ensuring compliance with safety regulations.

functions.label: Select a stock row or sort the list by column (Grid Row Select / Sort)
functions.description: When the operator clicks a row in the stock list, that row becomes highlighted for further actions. Clicking a column header toggles the sort order of that column between ascending and descending, and updates the header color to indicate the active sort. This sorting is performed instantly on the client without a database query, enabling rapid data exploration.

functions.label: Validate storage code against the database on entry (Storage Code Field Validation)
functions.description: As the operator enters a storage code in the filter field, the system immediately checks whether the code exists and is associated with the currently selected department. If the code is invalid, the field is highlighted or an error is shown, preventing search attempts with incorrect data. This real-time validation reduces input errors and ensures accurate stock retrieval.

functions.label: Validate employee code on entry (Employee Code Field Validation)
functions.description: When the operator types an employee code, the system performs an immediate lookup against the database to confirm the code exists. This validation helps prevent misspelled or non-existent employee codes, ensuring that subsequent stock searches by custodian are reliable.

functions.label: Validate department code and reset dependent fields (Department Code Field Validation)
functions.description: Upon entering a department code, the system validates its existence in the database. If the department code is changed, the storage code and related fields are automatically cleared to ensure configuration consistency. This validation maintains data integrity and prevents mismatched filter combinations.

functions.label: Navigate to the 8 target screens reached from this feature

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder MDI child window (w_hokanko_zaiko_list) where the warehouse operator can search stock items by storage code, employee, and department; view a stock list DataWindow; export to Excel; open bulk or single-row custodian reassignment popups; print Poison/Deleterious Substances Ledgers; and switch between stock list and movement history tabs, with real-time field validation against the database.
business_context.target_state: A React stock management page (<StockListManager />) backed by REST microservices exposing GET /api/v1/stocks (search), POST /api/v1/stocks/export (Excel), POST /api/v1/stocks/ledger (print), and POST /api/v1/stocks/assign (bulk/row reassignment), with an inline movement-history tab, server-side validation, and atomic transaction for custodian updates.

success_criteria: All search queries must use parameterised statements to prevent SQL injection.
Bulk custodian reassignment must execute within a single database transaction with rollback on any failure.
Stock list export to Excel must complete within 5 seconds for up to 1000 records.

user_stories.title: Bulk Reassign Custodian for Stock Items
user_stories.i_want_to: select multiple stock items, stage them in a bundle, enter a new custodian, and reassign ownership in a single batch transaction
user_stories.so_that: I can efficiently transfer custody of many chemicals when a department changes or a staff member leaves

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has opened the bulk reassignment popup, searched for and staged at least one stock item in the bundle grid, and entered a valid new assignee code that passes department match validation (or source department is R90)
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Update button after confirming the dialog
acceptance_criteria.then: the system updates the custodian and department for each staged item in a single atomic transaction, displays a success message, and optionally prompts to print the hazardous substances ledger if any item originated from R90

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has staged items but the new assignee code field is blank
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Update button
acceptance_criteria.then: the system shows an error message 'New assignee is required' and does not proceed

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has staged items and entered a new assignee whose department differs from a non-R90 source item's department
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Update button
acceptance_criteria.then: the system blocks the update and displays a department mismatch error

acceptance_criteria.given: one of the staged rows fails to update due to a database constraint or the row being concurrently modified
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Update button and a database constraint or concurrent modification error occurs
acceptance_criteria.then: the entire batch is rolled back and a failure message is displayed, leaving all records in their original state

user_stories.technical_notes: Legacy: w_hokanko_zaiko_tanto (opened from cb_tanto_chg). Staging via drag-and-drop or cb_dwn. Embedded SQL loop with FATRA transaction; f_commit/f_rollback. R90 department bypass logic. Inherits from w_fa_ances_infree.
user_stories.migration_hint: Implement as React modal <BulkReassignDialog>. Backend: PUT /api/v1/stocks/reassign/bulk with transactional service using @Transactional. Enforce server-side role check.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All updates in the batch must execute within a single database transaction with full rollback on any failure.
Every custodian reassignment must be logged with the new assignee, timestamp, and the previous custodian for audit purposes.

user_stories.title: Reassign Custodian for a Single Selected Stock Item
user_stories.i_want_to: directly open a popup pre-filled with a selected stock item's details and assign a new custodian to that single record
user_stories.so_that: I can quickly correct an individual custodian error without going through the bulk workflow

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has selected a row in the stock list grid and the selected-row reassign button is enabled, and the popup opens pre-filled with the item's details; the user has entered a valid new assignee code (defaulting to current user) and passes department validation (or source is R90)
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Update button in the popup
acceptance_criteria.then: the selected stock item's custodian and department are updated, a success message is shown, the popup closes, and, if the item was from R90, a ledger print prompt is optionally shown

acceptance_criteria.given: the user leaves the new assignee field blank
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks Update
acceptance_criteria.then: an error message 'New assignee is required' is displayed and the operation is blocked

acceptance_criteria.given: the popup is pre-filled with an item whose source department is R90
acceptance_criteria.when: the user selects a new assignee from a different department and updates
acceptance_criteria.then: the reassignment succeeds without department mismatch error, and the ledger print prompt is offered

user_stories.technical_notes: Legacy: w_hokanko_zaiko_tanto2, opened via cb_tanto_chg2. Receives stock row key via is_parm. Auto-fills current user as new assignee from g_tantocd. Embedded SQL UPDATE with FATRA transaction.
user_stories.migration_hint: React modal component <SingleReassignDialog> using route state. Backend PUT /api/v1/stocks/{compositeKey}/reassign. Preserve R90 bypass logic in service layer.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: The update must be atomic; if the ledger insert fails for an R90 item, the stock update must be rolled back.

results.module_business_description: Governs the lifecycle tracking, subdivision, stocktaking, and regulatory documentation of chemical inventories across development storage locations. Ensures compliance with poison and deleterious substance controls through batch and lot management, weight monitoring, and integrated ledger reporting.

features.title: Management Ledger Print
features.description: Provides a print dialog where users can filter and print a management ledger report by year, month, optional staff, and locker, then dispatch the report to a printer.

functions.label: Prepare the kanrisheet print form for data input (Screen Open)
functions.description: When the user opens the Management Ledger Print window, the dialog initializes the year and month fields, resets the staff and locker pickers, and sets focus for immediate data entry. This allows the user to quickly begin specifying the report criteria.

functions.label: Validate and print the kanrisheet ledger report (Print Button Click)
functions.description: After the user enters a year and month and optionally selects a staff member or locker, the system validates the mandatory inputs and retrieves the corresponding report data. The validated data is then dispatched to the printer, delivering the management ledger printout.

functions.label: Dismiss the kanrisheet print dialog without printing (Close Button Click)
functions.description: When the user clicks the Close button, the window closes and returns an empty result to the calling parent window. This cancels the print operation and navigates the user back to the previous screen without producing a report.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder modal dialog (w_hokanko_kanrisheet_print) where the user enters a year and month, optionally selects a staff member and locker, then clicks Print to retrieve and print the kanrisheet ledger report.
business_context.target_state: A React print dialog component (<LedgerPrintDialog />) backed by GET /api/v1/kanrisheet/report?year=&month=&staff=&locker=, generating a PDF report via a print service.

srs_section_scope: S.3 all controls: sle_year, sle_month, ddlb_staff, ddlb_locker, cb_print, cb_close
S.4 validation rule: VAL-007-01 (year/month input validation)

S.5 Event #2: Print Button Click — validate inputs, retrieve kanrisheet data, dispatch to printer

user_stories.technical_notes: Legacy PowerBuilder response window w_hokanko_kanrisheet_print. Print button cb_yes.clicked triggers validation of sle_year/sle_month, then dw_print.Retrieve() with dynamic SQL injection via sqlpreview event (concatenates uo_tanto.sle_code.Text and uo_hokanko.sle_code.Text directly into WHERE clause). Print dispatched via global function f_print(dw_print, False). Close button cb_no.clicked calls CloseWithReturn with empty s_pub_popdata. Screen open clears year/month fields, re-triggers NVO constructors, sets focus.
user_stories.migration_hint: Replace the modal dialog with a React <LedgerPrintDialog /> component. Expose POST /api/v1/kanrisheet/reports/print with JSON body { year, month, employeeCode?, warehouseCode?, departmentCode? }. Backend executes a parameterized query joined across M_DEVHOKAN_ENDZAIKO/M_DEVKAN/M_SYOHIN/M_SYAKAN/M_DEVHOKAN_HOKANKO tables with the prior-month snapshot rule (ADD_MONTHS(TO_DATE(...),-1)), then triggers a server-side PDF print service.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All database queries for report retrieval must use parameterised statements to prevent SQL injection (legacy concatenated raw input from uo_tanto/uo_hokanko into SQL).
Every print request must be logged with user identity, timestamp, and the provided filter parameters (year, month, staff, locker) to maintain a compliance audit trail.

results.module_business_description: Governs the lifecycle tracking, subdivision, stocktaking, and regulatory documentation of chemical inventories across development storage locations. Ensures compliance with poison and deleterious substance controls through batch and lot management, weight monitoring, and integrated ledger reporting.

features.title: Warehouse Ledger Item Search, Selection, and Print
features.description: Enables warehouse operators to search warehouse ledger items by employee, warehouse, and period, manage row selection via checkboxes, and print selected rows as ledger sheets. Supports switching between Month-End and Mid-Month data views and external employee/warehouse lookups.
features.source: SRS UIBlueprint w_hokanko_dgdai_list, S.5 Events #1-#11 (focal entrypoint)

functions.label: Search warehouse ledger items by employee, warehouse, and period (Search)
functions.description: Allows the warehouse operator to retrieve warehouse ledger items for the active tab (Month-End or Mid-Month) by specifying employee, warehouse, and optionally year/month on Month-End tab. The system loads matching rows into the grid for selection and printing.

functions.label: Reset search form and both grids to empty (Clear)
functions.description: Clears all entered search criteria and empties both the Month-End and Mid-Month grid tables. This provides a clean slate for a new search session without closing the window.

functions.label: Select all rows on the active tab (Select All On)
functions.description: Marks every row in the currently displayed ledger grid as selected for subsequent actions like printing. The selection is in-memory and will be lost on the next data retrieval.

functions.label: Deselect all rows on the active tab (Select All Off)
functions.description: Unchecks all row selection checkboxes on the active tab, clearing any current selection. This is an in-memory operation and selections will be reset after the next search.

functions.label: Toggle selection state of highlighted rows (Toggle Selection)
functions.description: Inverts the check mark on each row that is currently highlighted in the active grid. This allows quick switching of a subset of rows without affecting others; the change is not persisted.

functions.label: Print warehouse ledger sheets for selected rows (Ledger Print)
functions.description: Initiates printing of ledger sheets for the rows that have a checked checkbox. The system compiles the data, asks the user to confirm, and then sends the job to the printer; rows where a product master lookup fails are excluded and usage is printed as zero.

functions.label: Sort grid data by clicking column header (Grid Header Sort)
functions.description: Allows the user to click any column header in the active grid to sort the displayed rows by that column in ascending or descending order. The sort is performed on the client side without a new database query, and clicking the same header again toggles the sort direction.

functions.label: Look up employee code via modal search (Employee Double-Click Lookup)
functions.description: Opens a separate modal window where the operator can search for and select an employee code. The chosen code is then inserted into the employee filter field on the main search form, aiding accurate data entry.

functions.label: Look up warehouse code via modal search (Warehouse Double-Click Lookup)
functions.description: Opens a separate modal window to search for and select a warehouse code. The selected code is placed into the warehouse filter field, helping the operator quickly find the correct warehouse for the search.

functions.label: Close the warehouse ledger window and return (Close)
functions.description: Closes the current warehouse ledger item window and navigates the user back to the parent window. This ends the current session, discarding any unsaved selections.

functions.label: Switch between Month-End and Mid-Month ledger tabs (Tab Switch)
functions.description: Allows the operator to toggle between two ledger views: Month-End and Mid-Month. Switching changes the active grid displayed, and the system resets the sort state on the previously active tab, ensuring a fresh view.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder MDI child window (w_hokanko_dgdai_list) where warehouse operators can search for warehouse ledger items by employee, warehouse, and period (year/month on Tab 1), manage row selection via checkboxes, print ledger sheets for selected rows, and switch between Month-End and Mid-Month tabs. Employee and warehouse lookups open external modal popups (w_pub_pop_syainno, w_pop_devhokanko).
business_context.target_state: A React warehouse ledger management page (<WarehouseLedgerManager />) backed by REST microservices exposing GET /api/v1/warehouse-ledger/query with employee, warehouse, and date filters, a client-side selection mechanism with print generation via a dedicated print microservice, and tabbed Month-End/Mid-Month views. Employee and warehouse lookups are replaced by auto‑complete API endpoints.

user_stories.technical_notes: Legacy artifact: w_hokanko_dgdai_list (MDI child window) with two tabbed grids — dw_1 bound to dw_hokanko_endzaiko_list (Month-End stock, Tab 1) and dw_2 bound to dw_hokanko_d_zaiko_list (Mid-Month movements, Tab 2). Search header contains: sle_year (year, limit 4), sle_month (month, auto zero-padded), sle_syainno (employee code, double-click opens w_pub_pop_syainno popup), sle_hokankocd (warehouse code, double-click opens w_pop_devhokanko popup), dw_dev (development room dropdown bound to ddl_hokan_dev/ddw_hokan_dev). Search trigger via cb_retrieve (inherited from w_fa_ances_infree) calls u_retrieve on the active grid, which validates year/month on Tab 1 before executing Retrieve(). sqlpreview events on both grids dynamically rebuild the SQL WHERE clause using string concatenation from filter field values — parameterised query anti-pattern. Client-side sort via fw_sort_text() / fw_sort_text2() on column header click calls SetSort() + Sort(). FATRA custom Transaction Object used instead of default SQLCA. Tab switch via tab_1.selectionchanged swaps i_datawinname pointer between idw_1/idw_2 and resets sort state. Clear via cb_cancel triggers u_search_clear which blanks all filters and resets both grids.
user_stories.migration_hint: React <WarehouseLedgerManager /> component with a tabbed search interface (Month-End / Mid-Month tabs). Month-End tab requires year/month inputs with client-side validation; Mid-Month tab has no period filter. Backend microservice exposes GET /api/v1/mod-hokan/dgdai-list/endzaiko?year={year}&month={month}&employeeCode={code}&devRoomCode={code}&warehouseCode={code} (Tab 1) and GET /api/v1/mod-hokan/dgdai-list/dzaiko?employeeCode={code}&devRoomCode={code}&warehouseCode={code} (Tab 2). All queries must use server-side parameterised WHERE clauses — never concatenate user input into SQL. Replace w_pub_pop_syainno and w_pop_devhokanko modal popups with inline typeahead/autocomplete components backed by GET /api/v1/employees/search?q= and GET /api/v1/warehouses/search?devRoomCode={code}&q=. Client-side grid sort via React Table or AG Grid with multi-column sort. Development room dropdown populated from GET /api/v1/mod-hokan/dev-departments. Replace FATRA Transaction Object with a dedicated Spring DataSource or read-only @Transactional boundary per request.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All database queries for ledger item search must use parameterised statements or an ORM with bind variables to prevent SQL injection. The legacy sqlpreview events construct WHERE clauses via string concatenation of user-supplied filter text — this anti-pattern must not be replicated.

user_stories.technical_notes: Legacy artifact: cb_print button on w_hokanko_dgdai_list (overrides ancestor with full custom logic — no CALL SUPER). Print workflow: (1) Guard clause aborts silently if active grid RowCount() < 1 or zero rows have selectflg='1'. (2) Computes print period label as String(f_sysdate(),'YYYY年MM月分') — uses current system date, NOT the searched year/month. (3) Resets hidden dw_print DataWindow (bound to dw_devhokan_kanrisheet). (4) Loops every row of i_datawinname; for rows with selectflg='1', executes embedded SELECT NVL(DOKUFLG,'0'), NVL(GEKIFLG,'0') INTO :ls_dokuflg,:ls_gekiflg FROM M_SYOHIN WHERE SYOHINCD=:ls_syohincd USING FATRA. If FATRA.Sqlcode <> 0, row is silently skipped (Continue). Resolved rows are inserted into dw_print via InsertRow(0)+SetItem(): maps jyuryo to both ukeire (received) and jyuryo (stock), hard-codes shiyouryo (usage)=0, memo=''. (5) After loop, if dw_print.RowCount() < 1 aborts silently. (6) Displays MessageBox('毒劇物管理台帳を印刷しますか？', Question!, YesNo!, 1); aborts on No (return value 2). (7) Calls f_print(dw_print, False) to spool the print job. Selection controls: rb_on (Select All On) loops all rows setting selectflg='1'; rb_off sets selectflg='0'; cb_selectchg (Toggle) iterates only highlighted rows via GetSelectedRow() and inverts selectflg. selectflg is a client-side computed column ('0' as selectflg), never persisted to database.
user_stories.migration_hint: React grid component with checkbox column and bulk-select toolbar (Select All / Deselect All / Toggle Highlighted buttons). Print endpoint: POST /api/v1/mod-hokan/dgdai-ledger/print with body { selectedRowIds: [...] }. Backend service: (1) validate row IDs exist, (2) for each selected row, resolve toxic/deleterious flags from product master via GET /api/v1/products/{productCode}/hazard-flags or a batch lookup, (3) configure skip-vs-error policy for missing products (match legacy silent-skip or introduce explicit warning), (4) assemble the print payload mapping weight→receivedAmount and weight→stockWeight, usageAmount=0, periodLabel from request timestamp, (5) generate PDF ledger using Apache PDFBox or a templating engine (e.g. Thymeleaf + Flying Saucer), (6) return the PDF as a downloadable stream. Frontend shows confirmation modal before triggering the print API call. Replace f_print() with server-side PDF generation. Consider adding an audit log entry for every print operation capturing user identity, timestamp, and selected row count.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Every print operation of the toxic and deleterious substance management ledger must be persisted to an audit log with the authenticated user's identity, timestamp, number of rows printed, and the identifiers of any rows silently skipped due to missing product master data. This is a regulatory compliance document and its generation must be traceable.

features.title: Month-End Inventory List Search, Clear, Excel Export, and Close
features.description: Enables users to search, reset filters, export to Excel, and close the end-of-month inventory list within the inventory operations module.

functions.label: Retrieve filtered month-end inventory records (Search)
functions.description: The user specifies filter criteria to view month-end inventory records. Triggering the search validates inputs, resets the sort order, and retrieves matching rows into the grid. The row-delete button is then enabled or disabled based on the result set.

functions.label: Reset search criteria and grids to initial state (Clear)
functions.description: The user clears all search input fields and returns both data grids to their empty, default condition. The system also resets the job date control and sets the input focus there, ready for a fresh search.

functions.label: Export grid data to a formatted Excel file (Excel Export)
functions.description: The user exports the currently displayed inventory rows to an XLSX file. The system copies the grid contents into a staging buffer, prompts for a save location, and then uses OLE Automation to apply formatting and headers before finalising the document.

functions.label: Close the inventory window and return to main menu (Close)
functions.description: The user closes the month-end inventory list window to end the current session on that screen. This action returns the user to the parent MDI frame, enabling navigation to other parts of the application.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder window (w_hokanko_endzaiko_list) where inventory managers can filter and view month-end inventory records in a DataWindow grid, reset search criteria, export data to Excel using OLE Automation, and close the window to return to the parent MDI frame.
business_context.target_state: A React inventory list page (<MonthEndInventoryList />) backed by REST microservices providing GET /api/v1/month-end-inventory with filter parameters, and a POST /api/v1/month-end-inventory/excel export endpoint for Excel generation, with modern UI state management for clear and navigation.

user_stories.title: Search and Reset Month-End Inventory Records
user_stories.i_want_to: enter optional filter criteria, retrieve matching month-end inventory records, and clear all filters to start a new search
user_stories.so_that: I can locate relevant inventory data for a given period and easily reset the search to refine or broaden my query

acceptance_criteria.given: the month-end inventory list screen is open and the user has entered optional filter values (job date, product code, staff number, dev room code, storage code)
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Search button
acceptance_criteria.then: the system retrieves and displays matching inventory records in the grid and enables the Excel export option

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has entered filter criteria that do not match any records
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Search button
acceptance_criteria.then: the system displays an empty grid and shows an informational message indicating no matching information was found

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has performed a previous search and filled some filter fields
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Clear button
acceptance_criteria.then: all filter fields are emptied, the grid is cleared, and the job date dropdown is reset to its default state with focus placed on it

user_stories.technical_notes: PowerBuilder window w_hokanko_endzaiko_list; Search triggered by cb_retrieve::clicked (overrides ancestor pipeline u_retchek → u_sort_reset → u_retrieve). Dynamic filter construction occurs in dw_data::sqlpreview, which builds a WHERE clause from five optional SingleLineEdit fields (sle_syohincd, sle_syainno, sle_devcd, sle_hokanko) plus the dw_jobdt dropdown value, then injects ORDER BY nine key columns. Clear execution is in cb_cancel::clicked via u_search_clear that resets all inputs and grids. Grid ReadOnly is forced on open.
user_stories.migration_hint: Replace with a React <MonthEndInventoryList /> page calling GET /api/v1/month-end-inventory?jobDate={date}&productCode={code}&staffNo={no}&devRoomCode={code}&storageCode={code}. Clear resets local filter state without a backend call. Ensure all dynamic WHERE conditions are replaced with parameterised query placeholders in the API layer.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All database queries must use parameterised statements to prevent SQL injection.

user_stories.title: Export Month-End Inventory to Excel
user_stories.i_want_to: export the currently displayed inventory data to a formatted Excel (.xlsx) file
user_stories.so_that: I can share the month-end inventory information with colleagues or use it for offline reporting

acceptance_criteria.given: the grid contains at least one row of inventory data
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Excel Export button and selects a destination file path
acceptance_criteria.then: a new .xlsx file is created at the chosen location with a formatted header row containing the search criteria, column headers in Japanese, and the data rows with appropriate numeric and date formatting, and a success message is displayed

acceptance_criteria.given: the user attempts to save the export file with a file name that already exists
acceptance_criteria.when: the user confirms the overwrite in the dialog
acceptance_criteria.then: the existing file is replaced with the new export and a success message is shown; if the user cancels the overwrite dialog, the export is aborted and no file is written

acceptance_criteria.given: the grid is empty (no rows returned from the last search or the screen has just been opened)
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Excel Export button
acceptance_criteria.then: the system displays a message informing the user that there is no data to export and does not open a file save dialog

user_stories.technical_notes: PowerBuilder window w_hokanko_endzaiko_list, cb_excel::clicked event. It uses OLE Automation to interact with Excel.Application: copies the current rows from dw_data into a hidden DataWindow dw_excel, prompts the user for a save path with GetFileSaveName, saves the raw XLSX, then opens the file via OLE to apply formatting (header rows, numeric format ##0.0000 for content volume/weight/usage, date format YYYY/MM/DD for updated column, text format @ for headers). The entire OLE block is wrapped in TRY-CATCH (OLERuntimeError) with FINALLY ensuring OLE handle destruction.
user_stories.migration_hint: Replace with a server-side Excel generation endpoint POST /api/v1/month-end-inventory/export that accepts the same filter criteria as the search, queries the data on the server, builds an XLSX using Apache POI, and streams the binary file with a Content-Disposition header. Remove all client-side OLE dependencies.

features.title: Shelf Stocktaking Search, Launch, and Report Navigation
features.description: Enables warehouse operators to search shelf stocktaking records by year and month, launch the inventory stocktake data‑entry screen subject to a role permission check, generate stocktake reports, and navigate to related functions through command buttons and keyboard shortcuts. Dormant dev room code features remain inaccessible in the current UI state.
features.source: SRS UIBlueprint (w_hokanko_tana), S.5 Events #1–#8 – search, clear, close, stocktake launch, report output, dev room code popup/validation, and enter‑key simulation.

functions.label: Search shelf stocktaking records by year and month (cbSearch_Click)
functions.description: The user enters a year and month into the search fields and clicks the Search button. The system validates the input, zero-pads the month value, and retrieves matching shelf stocktaking records for display. This enables warehouse operators to quickly locate stocktaking data for a specific period.

functions.label: Launch inventory stocktake data-entry screen (cbInventoryStocktakeLaunch_Click)
functions.description: The user clicks the inventory stocktake button to open the stocktake data-entry screen. The system first checks that the current user has the required role permission (DEVCD = "R90") before proceeding. Only authorized operators can initiate the stocktaking process, maintaining data security.

functions.label: Validate development room code against master data (ue_devcd_validate)
functions.description: An internal validation routine compares the provided development room code against master data. This event is currently dormant and not triggered in the user interface because the associated input control is hidden. It exists as a safeguard if the field were to be exposed in a future configuration.

functions.label: Reset search fields and grid (cbClear_Click)
functions.description: The user clicks the Clear button to reset the search inputs and empty the displayed data grid. The action delegates to a shared clear routine, providing a fast way for operators to start a new search without manually clearing each field. This improves efficiency when switching between queries.

functions.label: Close the stocktaking search window (cbClose_Click)
functions.description: The user clicks the Close button to exit the shelf stocktaking search screen. This closes the current window, returning the user to the parent application workspace. It provides a standard and intuitive way to finish the search task.

functions.label: Open printable stocktake report window (cbReport_Click)
functions.description: The user clicks the stocktake report button to generate a printable stocktake report. This action opens a dedicated report window, which handles the report generation and print preview. Operators can then review and print the stocktaking results for physical verification or record-keeping.

functions.label: Select development room code from lookup popup (sle_devcd_DblClick)
functions.description: Double-clicking the hidden development room code field would display a shared code‑lookup popup, allowing the user to select a valid code. This event is currently dormant because the input field is hidden from the user interface. If later exposed, it would enable code‑assisted entry for the development room field.

functions.label: Activate focused button with the Enter key (w_fa_ances_infree_Key)
functions.description: Pressing the Enter key while a command button is focused triggers that button’s action, as if the user had clicked it. This global key handler makes the application more keyboard‑friendly, allowing rapid navigation and command execution without switching between mouse and keyboard. It streamlines the workflow for power users.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder MDI child window (w_hokanko_tana) where warehouse operators search shelf stocktaking records by year and month, launch the inventory stocktake data‑entry screen (gated by role R90), generate stocktake reports, and navigate using command buttons with a global Enter‑key handler. Two dormant events for dev room code lookup and validation are present but unreachable because the associated input control is hidden.
business_context.target_state: A React shelf stocktaking dashboard (<ShelfStocktakingManager />) backed by REST endpoints for search (GET /api/v1/shelf‑stocktaking?year=&month=), stocktake session launch (POST /api/v1/shelf‑stocktaking/sessions), and report generation (POST /api/v1/shelf‑stocktaking/reports), with role‑based access control, keyboard navigation, and modern input validation.

features.title: Shelf (Tana) Report Printing
features.description: Provides a print dialog for shelf (tana) reports, allowing users to set filter criteria, dynamically rebuild SQL WHERE/ORDER BY clauses, retrieve data, and dispatch physical print. The window remains open after printing to allow successive print jobs.
features.source: SRS UIBlueprint — w_hokanko_tana_print (focal entrypoint), S.5 Events #1-#4

functions.label: Retrieve and print shelf report with applied filters (Print Button Click)
functions.description: The user clicks the Print button after setting filter criteria. The system validates inputs, retrieves the report data dynamically, and dispatches the report to the physical printer. The dialog remains open so the user can adjust criteria and print again without reopening.

functions.label: Initialize print dialog with default filter values (Window Open)
functions.description: When the print dialog first opens, the system automatically sets default filter criteria and connects to the database transaction objects. It also places focus in the first input field, ready for user interaction. This initialization occurs once per dialog opening, ensuring consistent starting state.

functions.label: Dynamically rebuild report query based on filters (SQL Preview Rebuild)
functions.description: Before fetching report data, the system automatically reconstructs the SQL WHERE and ORDER BY clause to reflect the current filter criteria entered by the user. This ensures the retrieved dataset matches the desired filters without manual query editing. It runs as a server-side step embedded within the data retrieval process.

functions.label: Close the print dialog and return to parent (Close Button Click)
functions.description: When the user clicks the Close button, the print dialog closes immediately without any confirmation prompt and returns no data to the parent screen. This allows the user to abandon the print operation and navigate back to the previous interface.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder print dialog window (w_hokanko_tana_print) where users set filter criteria, trigger report data retrieval, and dispatch physical print. The dialog initializes default filters, dynamically constructs SQL WHERE/ORDER BY clauses, and remains open after printing for repeated operations.
business_context.target_state: A React print dialog component (<ShelfPrintDialog />) calling POST /api/v1/reports/shelf to submit filter parameters and generate the report, with server-side report generation and client-side print preview.

success_criteria: All SQL WHERE/ORDER BY clause construction must use parameterised queries to prevent SQL injection (dynamic SQL assembly detected in S.5 Event #4).

user_stories.technical_notes: Legacy PowerBuilder UI: w_hokanko_tana_print. Print button cb_yes.clicked performs client-side validation of Year/Month/Classification, zero-pads single-digit months, then calls dw_print.Reset() and dw_print.Retrieve(). The hidden report DataWindow dw_print (based on uo_anc_dw, dataobject dw_hokanko_tana_print) fires the sqlpreview event to dynamically inject WHERE and ORDER BY clauses via raw string concatenation of user inputs. After retrieval, if RowCount() > 0 the global function f_print(dw_print, False) dispatches the physical print.
user_stories.migration_hint: Implement a React <ShelfPrintDialog> component posting filter criteria to POST /api/v1/reports/shelf. The backend should execute a parameterised query mapping year, month, optional dev room code, and classification flags, and return a PDF/print stream. Replace string-concatenated SQL with bind parameters to close the injection surface.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All database queries must use parameterised statements to prevent SQL injection. The legacy sqlpreview event concatenates unescaped user input directly into the WHERE clause.

results.module_business_description: Governs the lifecycle tracking, subdivision, stocktaking, and regulatory documentation of chemical inventories across development storage locations. Ensures compliance with poison and deleterious substance controls through batch and lot management, weight monitoring, and integrated ledger reporting.

features.title: Storage Shelf Inventory List Search, Excel Export, and Stock Count Navigation
features.description: Enables warehouse operators to search shelf inventory records, view results in a data grid, export the listing to Excel, and navigate to stock count entry and inventory print windows. Ancestor CRUD operations (update, insert, delete, row copy) are present but hidden in the current build.

functions.label: Initialize shelf inventory list and bind data (Window Open/Initialisation)
functions.description: When the window opens, the system binds the database transaction object, resets all DataWindows (grid and search fields), and seeds them with initial values. This prepares the operator to immediately begin searching for storage shelf inventory records.

functions.label: Search shelf inventory records by filter criteria (Search)
functions.description: The user enters search criteria such as code or name, then triggers the search (Alt+S shortcut). The system validates the filters, clears any previous results from the grid, and retrieves matching shelf inventory records from the database using dynamic SQL.

functions.label: Export shelf inventory grid to Excel file (Excel Export)
functions.description: The operator can export the displayed shelf inventory results to an Excel workbook. The system prompts for a save location, uses OLE automation to create an Excel instance, writes column headers and all grid rows, and saves the file.

functions.label: Update modified shelf inventory records (Update)
functions.description: This latent ancestor function validates changes, checks for null values, prompts for confirmation, and commits updates to the database using DataWindow Update. The Update button is hidden, so users cannot currently access this feature.

functions.label: Print shelf inventory details (Print)
functions.description: This hidden ancestor function allows printing of shelf inventory data after user confirmation and a pre-print hook. In the current build, the Print button is hidden, so this feature is not directly accessible.

functions.label: Insert a new row into the inventory grid (Row Insert)
functions.description: The system can add a blank row to the shelf inventory DataWindow grid, allowing entry of new records. After insertion, the row-copy and delete buttons become active, but the Insert button is hidden.

functions.label: Delete a selected row from the inventory grid (Row Delete)
functions.description: This function removes the currently selected row from the shelf inventory grid. If the grid becomes empty, it disables the row-copy and delete buttons. The Delete button is hidden, making this feature unreachable.

functions.label: Copy a selected row in the inventory grid (Row Copy)
functions.description: This function is an unimplemented stub intended to duplicate a selected shelf inventory row. No copying logic exists; the associated button is hidden, providing no business value.

functions.label: Print the current window screen (F12 Screen Print)
functions.description: Pressing F12 captures the contents of the active window and sends it to the printer. The specific print function is chosen based on modifier keys, allowing a quick screen print of the shelf inventory list.

functions.label: Reset shelf inventory search fields and grid (Clear)
functions.description: Using the Clear command (Alt+L), the operator can restore all search input fields to their default values and empty the results grid. This allows a fresh start for a new search.

functions.label: Close the inventory list window (Close)
functions.description: The window is closed via the Close action (Alt+X), removing the shelf inventory list from the workspace. This typically ends the current search session.

functions.label: Navigate to stock count entry screen (Stock Count Entry Navigation)
functions.description: This latent navigation function opens the stock count entry window (w_hokanko_tanaoroshi) with necessary parameters. It is meant to connect inventory lookup to stock counting, but the button is currently hidden and not accessible.

functions.label: Navigate to inventory print output screen (Inventory Print Navigation)
functions.description: This hidden function opens the inventory print window (w_hokanko_tana_print) with relevant parameters. It provides a path to generate or preview inventory printouts, but is not available in the current user interface.

functions.label: Press Enter to activate a focused button (Enter-Key Button Trigger)
functions.description: When a button on the window is focused, pressing the Enter key triggers its click event. This keyboard shortcut enables users to quickly execute actions like Search without using the mouse.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder MDI child window (w_hokanko_tana_list) where warehouse operators search shelf inventory records by code or name, view results in a DataWindow grid, export the listing to Excel via OLE, and navigate to stock count entry (w_hokanko_tanaoroshi) and inventory print (w_hokanko_tana_print) windows. Ancestor-inherited CRUD buttons (Update, Print, Insert, Delete, Copy) are hidden and not reachable in the current UI.
business_context.target_state: A React shelf management page (<ShelfListManager />) backed by GET /api/v1/shelf-inventory with search filters, Excel export via POST /api/v1/excel-export, and navigation to stock count and print modules. All database operations use parameterised queries and atomic transactions.

success_criteria: All database queries for shelf search must use parameterised statements to prevent SQL injection (dynamic SQL detected in search event).
Any shelf record modification in the ancestor update operation must execute within a single atomic transaction with rollback on failure.

Navigation buttons (cb_stock_count, cb_inventory_print) are also hidden and unreachable in the current UI.

user_stories.i_want_to: export the currently displayed shelf inventory results to an Excel file

features.title: Shelf Stocktake Snapshot Regeneration and Reconciliation
features.description: Allows the stocktake operator to enter a target year and month, trigger a full shelf stocktake snapshot regeneration by clearing the existing period and rebuilding from live inventory, and close the window when finished.

functions.label: Validate inputs and regenerate shelf stocktake snapshot (HOKAN-013-F1-FN1)
functions.description: The stocktake operator confirms the target year and month, triggering a validation that checks CASNO master completeness. The system deletes any existing snapshot for that period and regenerates it from live inventory data, committing all changes in one operation.

functions.label: Initialize snapshot regeneration screen with defaults (HOKAN-013-F1-FN2)
functions.description: When the screen opens, it presets the year and month fields to default values and clears any previously displayed data in the staging grid. The focus is placed on the first entry field, ready for operator input without loading any data initially.

functions.label: Close snapshot regeneration window (HOKAN-013-F1-FN3)
functions.description: The operator can exit the screen at any time without making changes or processing data. The screen closes and sends an empty payload back to the parent, indicating that no action was taken.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder window (w_hokanko_tanaoroshi) where the stocktake operator enters a target year and month, triggers a snapshot regeneration via a Yes click that validates inputs, empties the existing period snapshot, and repopulates it from live inventory using a custom transaction (FATRA) with a known commit-ordering defect; the window also supports a simple close action and an initialisation that sets default year/month and resets the staging grid.
business_context.target_state: A React shelf stocktake page (<TanaoroshiRegeneration />) backed by a REST microservice exposing POST /api/v1/tanaoroshi/regenerate that validates the year/month, deletes the prior snapshot within an atomic transaction, and rebuilds it from the inventory event stream; the close redirects away and initialisation loads default fiscal period.

success_criteria: All multi-step database operations during snapshot regeneration must execute within a single atomic transaction with automatic rollback on any failure, eliminating the legacy double-commit defect.
Year and month inputs must be validated server-side for correct fiscal period format before triggering batch deletion/insert.

bounding_box.zone_label_jp: 棚卸スナップショット再生成

srs_section_scope: S.3 all controls: sle_year (year input), sle_month (month input), dw_stocktake (staging grid), cb_yes (confirm/generate), cb_close (close window)
S.4 validation rules: (none explicitly documented; validation logic is embedded within Event #1)
S.5 Event #1 (Yes Click): Validate year/month, check CASNO master completeness, delete existing period snapshot, regenerate from live inventory, commit
S.5 Event #2 (Close Click): Close screen without processing
S.5 Event #3 (Window Open): Initialize year/month fields, reset staging grid, bind transaction object, set initial focus
features.condensation_note: Uses custom transaction FATRA; contains a double-commit ordering defect. The snapshot regeneration deletes the existing period data and repopulates from live inventory in a single user action.

user_stories.title: Regenerate Shelf Stocktake Snapshot
user_stories.i_want_to: enter a target year and month and trigger the regeneration of the monthly shelf stocktake snapshot
user_stories.so_that: I can maintain accurate stocktake records and enable period-over-period weight comparisons for hazardous-material inventory reconciliation

acceptance_criteria.given: the shelf stocktake snapshot regeneration screen is displayed with the year and month fields ready for input and the operator enters a valid 4-digit year (e.g., 2012) and a valid month (e.g., 12)
acceptance_criteria.when: the operator clicks the Yes button to confirm
acceptance_criteria.then: the system validates the inputs, checks CAS number completeness, deletes any existing snapshot for that period, regenerates the snapshot from live inventory, commits the changes, and displays a '処理が終了しました。' (Processing completed) message

acceptance_criteria.given: the operator leaves the year field empty and enters a month
acceptance_criteria.when: the operator clicks the Yes button
acceptance_criteria.then: the system displays an error message '年を入力して下さい。' (Please enter the year) and aborts processing without any data changes

acceptance_criteria.given: the operator enters a year but leaves the month field empty
acceptance_criteria.when: the operator clicks the Yes button
acceptance_criteria.then: the system displays an error message '月を入力して下さい。' (Please enter the month) and aborts processing without any data changes

acceptance_criteria.given: the operator enters a valid year and month but the master data contains products with missing CAS numbers
acceptance_criteria.when: the operator clicks the Yes button
acceptance_criteria.then: the system displays an error message listing the affected product codes and instructs the operator to register CAS numbers before proceeding, and does not perform any deletion or insertion

acceptance_criteria.given: the operator enters a valid year but a single-digit month (e.g., '3')
acceptance_criteria.when: the operator clicks the Yes button
acceptance_criteria.then: the system automatically zero-pads the month to two digits ('03'), processes the regeneration successfully, and displays the completion message

user_stories.technical_notes: Executes full snapshot regeneration in cb_yes.clicked event of w_hokanko_tanaoroshi.srw using embedded SQL: validates year/month, calls wf_chk_casno() for CASNO completeness, deletes existing period from SIL00.M_DEVZAIKO_HOKANTANA, recomputes weight-adjusted inventory via cursor tana with SUM(JYURYO*NVL(GENRITU,100)/100), and inserts rows into dw_tanaoroshi (bound to dw_hokanko_tana). Uses custom transaction object FATRA with a known double-commit ordering defect where f_commit is called before checking li_ret. Screen initialisation sets fields empty and focus.
user_stories.migration_hint: Create POST /api/v1/tanaoroshi/generate endpoint with a Spring @Transactional service that wraps the entire delete-and-insert operation in a single database transaction, performs CASNO validation via a separate service call, computes prior month date using Java time API, and returns a processed row count with completion message; use React <TanaoroshiRegeneration /> component to collect year/month input and trigger the API call.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All database operations (DELETE existing snapshot and INSERT regenerated rows) must execute within a single atomic transaction with full rollback on any step failure to prevent partial period data.

user_stories.i_want_to: review and document the four orphaned legacy artifacts (f_get_defaultprinter, f_parsetoarray, f_set_defaultprinter, s_hokanko_parm) as confirmed dead code for decommissioning
user_stories.so_that: the modernization backlog excludes these artifacts and avoids unnecessary reimplementation effort

acceptance_criteria.given: the migration engineer has access to the dead code analysis report for MOD-HOKAN and has reviewed the forensic evidence showing zero SQL, zero data persistence, and no callers found for the four artifacts
acceptance_criteria.when: the engineer marks all four orphaned artifacts as 'confirmed dead'
acceptance_criteria.then: the system records these artifacts as decommissioned and removes them from the active migration scope

acceptance_criteria.given: the dead code analysis report indicates ambiguous linkage for s_hokanko_parm (possible live usage in another MFU)
acceptance_criteria.when: the migration engineer attempts to mark all four artifacts as dead
acceptance_criteria.then: the system warns that s_hokanko_parm may still be in use and requires cross‑MFU reconciliation before decommissioning can be confirmed

acceptance_criteria.given: the migration engineer has marked all four artifacts as dead, and a subsequent full‑codebase call‑graph scan confirms no active callers exist
acceptance_criteria.when: the engineer finalizes the decommissioning decision
acceptance_criteria.then: the system permanently archives the artifacts and they no longer appear in migration reports

user_stories.technical_notes: Orphaned PowerBuilder global functions: f_get_defaultprinter (Windows Registry read, TRCE-IO‑f_get_defaultprinter‑L1), f_set_defaultprinter (Registry write), f_parsetoarray (PFC string utility), and structure s_hokanko_parm (device/depot parameters). None have embedded SQL or DataWindow bindings; all are isolated client‑side utilities with no external callers identified in the supplied payload.
user_stories.migration_hint: No modern equivalent required — decommission if call‑graph confirms dead code. If default‑printer discovery is still needed, re‑implement as a client‑side browser Print API, not a server endpoint.

user_stories.title: Retrieve OS Environment Variable Value
user_stories.i_want_to: call the GET endpoint with an environment variable name and receive its current value
user_stories.so_that: I can access machine-level configuration settings without re-implementing the environment variable lookup logic

acceptance_criteria.given: the environment variable 'TEMP' exists in the server's OS environment with a valid path
acceptance_criteria.when: the API consumer sends a GET request with the query parameter key=TEMP
acceptance_criteria.then: the system returns HTTP 200 with a JSON response containing the value field set to the environment variable's string value

acceptance_criteria.given: the required query parameter 'key' is missing from the request
acceptance_criteria.when: the API consumer sends a GET request without the key parameter
acceptance_criteria.then: the system returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with an error message indicating the missing parameter

acceptance_criteria.given: the requested environment variable name does not exist in the server's OS
acceptance_criteria.when: the API consumer sends a GET request with key=NONEXISTENT_VAR
acceptance_criteria.then: the system returns HTTP 200 with the value field containing an empty string, matching legacy behavior

user_stories.technical_notes: Legacy artifact: PowerBuilder global function f_get_osval (hokan/f_get_osval.srf). Uses GetContextService('Keyword', lcx_key) and GetContextKeywords() to read client-side OS environment variables. No SQL, no transaction object. Always returns first match or empty string on failure.
user_stories.migration_hint: Implement as a Spring Boot service method (e.g. EnvironmentLookupService.getValue(String key)) using System.getenv(). Replace the PB-specific ContextKeyword availability gate with Optional<String>. Publish as GET /api/v1/mod-hokan/sys-util-01/environment-variable?key={name}. Consider a modern validation layer to reject missing or empty keys.
